question: Does portable individual strength, rather than the Elo of the player's old team, correct live team forecasts after roster changes?
reference: deployed nba-multimarket-live-1.5.0 fit and T-60 availability; RUN071 plus extended columns (nba_live14b_20261025/data)
ratings: Separate ridge regressions of final margin and total on each player's actual regulation minutes / 48, signed home-minus-away for margin and added for total. Unpenalized intercept. Last 730 days strictly before Aug 1 of the season; weights halve every 180 days, normalized to mean 1. Ridge candidates 25 and 100. Coefficients are individual game-level associations, not causal RAPM or old-team Elo.
rotation: Last 20 appearances within 370 days follow the player across teams. Current official roster provides membership in live. Expected minutes = (5 * personal mean + own-team minutes over the last five current-season games)/(5 + number of those games), unknown player prior 12 minutes. Allocate exactly 240 minutes with cap 48 per player. Membership does not establish health. The model's existing availability remains separate.
correction: Compare expected current rotation to mean actual rotation of the team's last 20 games within 370 days. The individual margin and total coefficient differences yield changes in own/opponent expected points; multiply by weight in {0.25, 0.5, 1}. Update each team and total normal tail at the SAME reference line and keep the reference covariance. Winner log odds shift by the change in normal margin log odds; zero correction reproduces reference exactly.
chronology: Infer historical membership only from players seen in the team's last five games this season whose latest earlier appearance is still for that team. No current rosters retroactively applied. No current-season game means no observed roster and a zero correction. All same-day features built before any box of that day is observed. Live official rosters allow membership before debut, but that subgroup has no historical validation here.
selection: Choose ridge and weight by pooled Brier over winner, team points and total in 2024-25 (team fit on 2022-23 and 2023-24); team points counts as one market by averaging both sides per game, each of the three markets receives equal weight. Ties choose smaller weight then stronger ridge. No choice based on 2025-26.
evaluation: Apply chosen configuration unchanged to 2025-26 (reference team fit on 2023-24 and 2024-25). Report per-market Brier, log loss, bias, calibration slope/intercept, first 30 days, high turnover, source hashes and per-game rows. Descriptive retrospective; 2025-26 already observed for other questions, not an untouched holdout.
acceptance: Winner paired Brier 95% interval upper bound < 0, and neither team points nor total has a worsening with 97.5% interval lower bound > 0. Bootstrap dates, 800 replicates, seed 20261026. Rejected candidates stay out. Correcting current membership itself is a verified data correction, independent of this statistical acceptance test.
deployment: Versioned protocol, code/data/model hashes, refit from exact code, server comparison, real rehearsal, immutable old cohorts, rollback. Do not claim improved accuracy before measuring it. Add current-season completed games to the live strength fit only after they finish; research evaluation uses preseason fits and does not certify that online update.
limits: Whole-game minutes cannot distinguish individual effects perfectly from teammates
Historical current-season debut and offseason roster coverage is incomplete
Unknown players shrink to average and unknown minutes must be reported
A stronger roster does not guarantee a win
